LESSON: SORTING & GROUPING

Grade: PP1
Subject: MATHEMATICS ACTIVITIES
Strand: CLASSIFICATION
Topic 1.1: Sorting & grouping

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Sorting & grouping. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Which objects look alike?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify differences among objects in the environment to appreciate their similarities and differences
2. enjoy sorting and grouping objects in the environment
3. group objects according to a specific attribute to create sets of similar objects materials in their respective e) appreciate the materials corners. in the environment for their uniqueness and according to one attribute using diversity. ICT devices.

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. identify differences among objects in the environment to appreciate their similarities and differences
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to identify differences among objects in the environment to appreciate their similarities and differences. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. enjoy sorting and grouping objects in the environment
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to enjoy sorting and grouping objects in the environment. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. group objects according to a specific attribute to create sets of similar objects materials in their respective e) appreciate the materials corners. in the environment for their uniqueness and according to one attribute using diversity. ICT devices.
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to group objects according to a specific attribute to create sets of similar objects materials in their respective e) appreciate the materials corners. in the environment for their uniqueness and according to one attribute using diversity. ICT devices. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market in your county, count 10 mangoes. Put them in 2 groups of 5. That is sorting and grouping.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row. Write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and your parent gives you 5 more, you have 12 shillings. That is addition.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Sorting & grouping.
2. Explain Sorting & grouping to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Sorting & grouping.
4. Show that you can: identify differences among objects in the environment to appreciate their similarities and differences
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Sorting & grouping. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Which objects look alike?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. identify differences among objects in the environment to appreciate their similarities and differences
2. enjoy sorting and grouping objects in the environment
3. group objects according to a specific attribute to create sets of similar objects materials in their respective e) appreciate the materials corners. in the environment for their uniqueness and according to one attribute using diversity. ICT devices.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.
